messages:
alicia.s: Heads-up: multiple customers reporting 500/503s for hosted inference since 08:12 UTC. CS on call got three escalations in ~10m.

ben.cs: Customer reports: sudden spike in API errors, responses 500 with 'upstream worker exited'. They saw timeouts and retries. Billing noticed a token spike for one tenant.

alicia.s: I pulled logs from gateway for the window. Repeated upstream disconnects + container restarts. Suspect worker coredump.

ops-alert-bot: Deploybot: host-infer-pool-12 reported container restart for infer-runner pid=4221 at 2024-05-06T08:11:29Z (OOM killer).

diego.oncall: Oncall here. Can someone paste the latest runner stderr? Also which models were hot-swapped?

sarah.eng-runtime: Pasting trimmed log snippet:```
[08:11:28] infer-runner[4221]: CUDA error: out of memory (CUDA out of memory)
[08:11:28] infer-runner[4221]: Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f9a2c...
[08:11:28] infer-runner[4221]: Backtrace (most recent call first): 
  #0 0x7f9a2c1a kernel_attn.cu
  #1 0x7f9a3b2b serve_loop.cpp
  #2 0x55d0f4f main
```

kevin.infra: Host kernel logs show `oom_reaper` activity and container killed by cgroup OOM. GPU memory usage peaked at 98% on GPU0.

ben.cs: Customer says they were sending long streaming prompts + tool calls; model was a 70B open variant (quantized).

alicia.s: Short-term mitigations: 1) route this customer's traffic to CPU fallback pool, 2) enable graceful degradation to smaller model (32B), 3) temporarily reduce max_context for that tenant to limit mem growth. Can infra apply routing override?

diego.oncall: Applying a route override now: `route set --tenant acme-corp --fallback cpu-pool --priority=1000` — will take ~30s to propagate. Also lowering batch target for that pool.

sarah.eng-runtime: Repro notes: appears to happen during KV-prefetch + toolcall combination with large sequence lengths. Likely memory ballooning from prefetch + attention kernel. Repro steps we have so far:
  1) Send streaming prompt with ~256k tokens in chunks
  2) Trigger a toolcall that expands context (evals/call)
  3) Rapid multiplex QPS > 120

ben.cs: CS update: customer agreed to temporary reroute. They're upset about latency and impact on billing. Asked for ETA to fix.

kevin.infra: Started collecting coredump, nvcrash logs, `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` snapshot saved to s3://redwood-debug/1738456789/. Also grabbing container start env.

alicia.s: Can eng-runtime look for regression in kernel selection or recent quantization swap? Last deploy touched attn-optimizations.

sarah.eng-runtime: Noted a config change rolled 2d ago: `attn_kernel=fast_prefetch_v2` — rolling back to `fast_prefetch_v1` on the affected pool for now. Will monitor.

diego.oncall: After route override I see error rate drop for acme-corp from 12% -> 1.2%. Other tenants on same host still showing occasional restarts; isolating to pool-12.

ben.cs: Customer billing team flagged a credit request; CS asked for incident summary and ETA for a patch.

alicia.s: Next steps: (1) eng-runtime reproduces locally with KV-prefetch + long toolcall test harness (assigned to sarah), (2) infra will repro on staging with reduced mem headroom and collect full coredump (kevin), (3) CS to keep customer on CPU fallback and prepare credit email (ben).

sarah.eng-runtime: Assigned. Early hypothesis: quantized kernel + prefetch yields unchecked allocation in attn kernel, leading to OOM -> illegal mem access -> SIGSEGV. If confirmed, hotfix may be a bounds-check + fallback to safer kernel. Patch timeline: 24-48h if reproducible.

diego.oncall: Marking incident P1. If we see more host restarts, we'll trigger capacity eviction / drain for pool-12.

alicia.s: Thanks all. I'll update the incident doc with links to s3 logs and customer timeline.

ben.cs: Customer call scheduled 09:00 UTC to explain mitigation and next steps.

ops-alert-bot: Incident channel updated: status=investigating, severity=P1, incident_id=INC-1738456789.
